title: Getting Qualified: Driver CPC Parts 1 to 4
whatItIs: To drive a lorry professionally you need a full car licence, a provisional lorry licence and the full Driver CPC: 5 tests in 4 parts. Then 35 hours of training every 5 years.

keyFacts.text: You MUST have the full Driver CPC if driving a lorry is your main job.

keyFacts: Start with a provisional licence: forms D2 and D4 (medical).
Pass part 1 before booking 3a and 3b, and part 2 before part 4.
Pass 3b within 6 months of passing 3a, or take 3a again.
Pass 3a and 3b within 2 years of passing your first theory part.

keyFacts.text: You MUST carry your Driver CPC card when driving professionally: £50 fixed penalty without it.

visual.caption: The route to a full Driver CPC

items.title: Provisional licence
items.text: Forms D2 and D4 (medical) to DVLA. Free.

items.title: Part 2: case studies
items.text: 7 case studies on a computer. Pass: 40/50.

items.title: Part 3a: off-road exercises
items.text: 'S' reverse into a bay; uncouple and recouple if towing.

items.title: Part 3b: on-road driving
items.text: 1 hour of driving. Pass: 12 or fewer driving faults, no serious ones.

items.title: Part 4: demonstration
items.text: 5 topics. At least 15/20 in each, 80/100 overall.

onTheTest.question: You passed Driver CPC part 3a. How long do you have to pass part 3b?
onTheTest.why: Pass part 3b within 6 months of getting your part 3a certificate, or you'll need to pass part 3a again.

onTheTest.question: Which test must you pass before you can book Driver CPC part 4?
onTheTest.why: You must pass part 2 (case studies) before you can book part 4.

traps: Part 2 doesn't need part 1 first: book it once you have a provisional licence.
Driving not your main job? You may not need the full Driver CPC, but still pass parts 1, 3a and 3b.
